title: Dart effect patterns unreachable for external package calls
description:
Codex review finding from sutra/111. The DART_EFFECT_PATTERNS callee prefixes (dart:io::File, http::, dio::, sqflite::, etc.) require resolved call refs with target symbol IDs. But Dart external package calls like `http.get(...)` are classified as field access by ref context classification, and the resolver skips field-access refs. Effect enrichment is effectively a no-op for normal Dart code.

This is arguably a cross-language limitation — the effect pipeline assumes resolved call refs, which works for Rust (intra-crate calls resolve) but breaks for any language where external calls go unresolved.

Options:
1. Synthesize external callee names from Dart import aliases + member expressions before effect enrichment
2. Implement Dart-specific effect detection over imports + unresolved/member refs
3. Add an import-based heuristic: if a file imports `package:http`, mark it `effect:net` at file level"

acceptance_criteria.text: Dart member-expression calls (e.g. `http.get(...)`, `dio.post(...)`) whose object identifier matches a known import-derived package name get effect attributes (`effect:net`, `effect:fs`, `effect:db`) at symbol-level granularity
Only the function containing the call gets the effect attribute — not the entire file
Existing resolved-callee effect enrichment path (Rust, intra-crate Dart) is unchanged
DART_EFFECT_PATTERNS callee_prefixes remain the single source of truth for package→effect mapping
No schema migration required — works with existing imports table
Reuses external_crate_of_import() or equivalent for package name extraction

execution_record: Implemented as planned, then Codex adversarial review surfaced two real issues: (1) tools/review.rs had a parallel attribute-building path that didn't include the new Dart enrichment — fixed by extracting shared helpers `enrich_all_effects()` and `dart_effect_packages()`, (2) Pattern B (class-name matching for dart:io::File etc.) was too broad — matched type annotations. Tightened to call/construction/field_access context kinds only. Both fixed in follow-up commit b10f6b5.
